rules.statement: Bullish structure is HH/HL, bearish structure is LL/LH; range is a third phase; structure applies on all timeframes.
In bullish structure a high is structurally relevant when it updates the prior high; in bearish structure a low is structurally relevant when it updates the prior low.
Breaking the protected structural point changes structure; after bullish structure breaks below the last HL bearish structure is expected, and vice versa for a bearish break above the relevant LH.
After bullish structure breaks and bearish structure forms, seek short when LH forms; after bearish structure breaks and bullish structure forms, seek long when HL forms.
Range is sideways trading in a defined area; one source description uses the first high after the impulse and first low as boundaries; normal trend structure should be absent inside.
Trade range only after deviation outside a boundary; validate with reaction around 0.5; one setup is return after deviation then test of the zone that sent price back into range with CHOCH.
OB is the last candle before an imbalance/sharp impulse; the move must update a structural point; the OB must take some high/low or wick; body large, wicks small.
Imbalance is sharp impulsive movement leaving price inefficiency; mark the empty zone using neighboring candle shadows.
Breaker is an OB that took a high/low and was then impulsively broken with imbalance, followed by CHOCH.
Liquidity represents traders' stops and can be a trade target; EQH/EQL and trendline liquidity are liquidity concepts.
0.5 is equilibrium; relevant levels include 0.62, 0.705 and 0.79; OTE is the 0.705-0.79 zone and complements other setup evidence, especially OB.

SFP is a reversal pattern, originally three candles with optional fourth confirmation; it sweeps stops above/below a swing or range boundary and reverses without body acceptance beyond the swept area; context is mandatory; applies on all timeframes.

AMD is accumulation-manipulation-distribution; source discusses POIs around manipulation-to-distribution transition and a riskier manipulation entry with return speed, liquidity removal and volume considerations.
Use completed strict three-bar pivots: center high strictly above both neighboring highs is a swing high; center low strictly below both neighboring lows is a swing low.
rules.rationale: Needed to make HH/HL/LH/LL causal and deterministic; inherited from prior source-evidence process, not claimed as wording from Methodichka.

rules.statement: Publish BOS only after a completed candle body close beyond the protected structural level; wick-only excursions remain liquidity/sweep evidence, not BOS.
rules.rationale: Causal deterministic close semantics; source distinguishes false moves/body acceptance but does not supply one universal BOS equation.

rules.statement: For a three-candle sequence, bullish inefficiency exists when third-candle low is above first-candle high; bearish inefficiency exists when third-candle high is below first-candle low. The geometric gap uses those wick boundaries.
rules.rationale: Implements the source instruction to mark inefficiency using neighboring candle shadows without inventing a minimum size threshold.

rules.statement: Emit a raw bearish SFP candidate when a completed candle sweeps above an already-known structural/range level and closes back at/below that level; bullish is symmetric below the level. Do not claim final source-valid SFP until unresolved context/three-candle semantics are satisfied.
rules.rationale: Captures sweep plus body non-acceptance while preserving unresolved exact pattern geometry instead of rejecting it.

rules.statement: Initial detector universe is M15/H1/H4/D1; architecture must be reusable on every active timeframe and allow lower-TF expansion when data is available.
Before P&L, target >=365 actionable setup opportunities per coin-year across active timeframes; never fabricate trades; failure means SOURCE_FIDELITY_STOP and detector repair.
